newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Analysts see Bulgaria inflation fall in July.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see Bulgaria inflation fall in July.

text.p: Bulgaria's monthly consumer prices rose by 5.6 percent in May, up on government's expectations of zero, but economists say the underlying trend is positive and see inflation near zero in July and August.
"We see consistent lowering of the monthly inflation rate with the introduction of the currency board," Parvoleta Shtereva, emerging markets economist in ING Bank in London told Reuters.
The National Statistics Institute attributed the rise mostly to fresh fruit and vegetable prices which had a greater weight in the basket in May.
Fresh fruits rose by 22.1 percent in May month on month, vegetables rose 89 percent with potatoes posting the biggest price rise of 125 percent.
"If there are no further utility price rises, we can expect inflation in July and August to slow to around zero," said Kamen Kolchev, manager of Elana Financial Company on Sofia.

June inflation is expected to remain around three to five percent due to the slight devaluation of the lev, after last week's announcement that the lev will be pegged to the mark as anchor in the currency board system at a rate of 1,000, said Shtereva.
The lev traded at around 900 levs to the mark in the previous two months.
Bulgaria is expected to launch a restrictive currency board system on July 1 aimed to stabilise the volatile currency and shaky banks under a funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund.

The IMF deal and severe stabilisation measures helped the country dramaticaly bring down monthly inflation to 0.7 percent in April and 12 percent in March after political and economic instability triggered prices to a galloping 243 percent in February.
Monthly inflation traditionally falls in the summer season as farm produce prices go down.
Cumulative inflation for the first five months was 479.4 percent. Assumed annual inflation in the draft 1997 budget is 566 percent.
Under IMF agreement the government pledged to curb monthly inflation to two percent by year-end. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
